RFC4035-3-6.note: TestRFC4035_NoDNSSECAdditionalProcessing covers only the OPT-less query; the sentence also covers a query WITH an OPT whose DO bit is clear, which no unit sends, so the second arm of the condition is unproven (question 4)

RFC4035-3-8.note: TestRFC4035_CDCopiedADIgnored drives the real dnsserver.Authoritative harness: a CD=1 query must draw CD=1 and a CD=0 query CD=0, so both an always-clear and an always-set implementation go red

RFC4035-3-9.note: the negative asserts an AD=1 query draws a reply with AD clear through the real harness; the positive's answer-equality half runs over the answerOne test stub, which cannot vary, so the AD-echo assertion is the discriminating one

RFC4035-3.1.4.1-1.note: an apex DS query through geodns answerQuery under the real harness must return NOERROR, AA set, empty Answer, SOA in Authority, and no RA; an NXDOMAIN or REFUSED answer at the apex goes red; the negative pins that the no-data answer is not given for an out-of-zone name

RFC4035-3.1.6-2.note: single polarity: asserts AD clear on both the OPT-less and DO-set geodns replies, and ze authenticates nothing, so any AD-setting path goes red

RFC4035-3.1.6-4.note: single polarity: geodns serves zone data from the running configuration, not obtained by secure means, and the unit asserts it is never flagged authentic (AD clear) on either reply

RFC4035-3.1.6-5.note: single polarity: no configuration marks local data authentic, and the unit asserts AD clear on the geodns replies whatever the query's DO bit

RFC4035-4.1-1.note: Forbidden: a security-aware query sent without an OPT, or with DO clear. TestRFC4035_QueryCarriesEDNS0DOAndClearAD fatals on a missing OPT and errors on DO clear, but only under dnssec-validation strict. The row's own marker names permissive mode as security-aware too (SetEdns0(4096, validating) at resolver.go:261), and no tagged unit captures a permissive-mode query, so a regression that set DO only for strict stays green

RFC4035-4.1-4.note: Forbidden: an OPT whose sender's UDP payload size is not the size the resolver accepts. The unit pins opt.UDPSize() == 4096 under strict mode only; the clause 'the message size that it is willing to accept' is not tied to the receive side in this unit (the large-response acceptance is TestRFC4035_LargeUDPResponseAccepted, tagged RFC4035-4.1-2, not this id), and permissive mode, security-aware per the row's marker, sends no captured query

RFC4035-4.6-3.note: TestRFC4035_ResponseADBitDisregarded covers the AD bit only; the CD half of the sentence is untested (question 4); the negative's AD=1 reply is a SERVFAIL, which dnssecDecision rejects for its rcode alone, so it would stay green even if ze honoured AD=1 on a NOERROR answer (question 3)

RFC4035-4.9-1.note: an A+RRSIG answer must return exactly the A record and a DNSSEC-only answer (RRSIG, NSEC, DNSKEY) must yield no records and no error, so mishandling either way goes red
